summary: Implement on‑device OCR receipt scanning, replace typed dates with a calendar date picker, and add a full category management system (defaults, custom add, rename, hide, backup/restore). Provide pure‑logic OCR parsing (parseReceipt) and a categories module with encrypted storage, update the receipt entry and mileage entry screens to use react‑native‑paper‑dates, update the settings screen to manage categories, extend the backup format to include categories, add a Jest mock for expo‑text‑extractor, add unit tests for parseReceipt (8 realistic receipts) and for categories (defaults, add, duplicate, rename, hide, in‑use protection, backup round‑trip), and update ui_flow.json to reflect the new UI flow (date picker and category dropdown). All existing screens, flows, tests, and local‑first design remain unchanged and must continue to pass.
steps: Add a new module src/lib/ocr.ts exposing two async functions: recognizeReceiptText(uri: string): Promise<string> that calls expo-text-extractor (guarded by Platform.OS === 'web' to reject on web) and parseReceipt(text: string): ParsedReceipt that extracts optional {merchant, date, total, tax} using regexes for US date formats, total lines (TOTAL|AMOUNT DUE|BALANCE) and the first non‑trivial line for merchant.

Create a Jest mock at __mocks__/expo-text-extractor.ts that exports a mock function 'extract' which simply resolves with a predefined text string; this will allow the parseReceipt unit tests to run without native code.

Implement src/lib/categories.ts. Define DEFAULT_CATEGORIES array (the 13 categories from the task). Store mutable data under a single encrypted store key 'categories' with shape { custom: string[], hidden: string[], rename: Record<string,string> }. Export async functions: getAllCategories(store, { includeHidden = false }) → Array<{ id: string, name: string, hidden: boolean, custom: boolean }>, addCustomCategory(store, name) → string|null error, renameCategory(store, oldName, newName) → string|null error, hideCategory(store, name) → string|null error, isCategoryInUse(store, name) → Promise<boolean>, syncCategoriesWithReceipts(store) – scans receipts and adds missing receipt‑category strings as custom entries.

Extend src/lib/backup.ts: modify createBackup to also fetch categories data via categories.getAllCategories (include hidden/renamed/custom) and embed it in the backup JSON under a new top‑level key "categories". Update restoreBackup to read this key (if present) and write it back to the store using categories module functions. Adjust validateBackupStructure in src/lib/validation.ts to accept an optional "categories" object matching the shape used in backup.

Update src/screens/ReceiptEntryScreen.tsx: add a Scan button that calls recognizeReceiptText with the selected photo URI, then runs parseReceipt on the result. Pre‑fill the receipt form fields with the parsed values, display a helper text 'Check these details' next to each pre‑filled field, and mark those fields as un‑touched until the user edits them. If parseReceipt returns no data, show an alert 'No details could be extracted – please enter manually'. On web platforms, replace the Scan button with a disabled tooltip reading 'Scanning is available in the phone app'. Use the existing form components but replace the manual date TextInput with the react‑native‑paper‑dates DatePickerModal (imported from react-native-paper-dates) – default to today, disallow future dates for receipts.

Update src/screens/MileageEntryScreen.tsx: replace the typed date input with a DatePickerModal (same library) and set its default to today; also ensure future dates are allowed for mileage (no restriction).

Update src/screens/SettingsScreen.tsx: add a new 'Categories' section. Use the categories module to list current categories (display name = renamed if applicable). For each default/custom category provide actions to rename (inline edit), hide (toggle), and for custom categories also allow deletion (only if not used by any receipt – otherwise show the hide option). Add a UI element 'Add category…' that opens a dialog to type a new name (1‑40 chars, case‑insensitive duplicate check). Persist changes via the categories module. Ensure the UI respects the 'hidden' flag (hidden categories are not shown in the receipt entry dropdown).

Update ui_flow.json: modify the primary receipt‑entry flow to reflect the new UI – replace the step where the user types a date with a step "Select receipt date" (calendar picker) and replace the category text input step with "Select receipt category" (dropdown). Add an optional step after the receipt scan where the user can tap "Add custom category" if the desired category is not listed. Ensure the flow still ends with the Save button.

Add __tests__/ocr.test.ts: write at least eight realistic receipt text fixtures (grocery, fuel, restaurant with tip, hardware store, online order, faded/partial text, receipt with several dates, receipt with no total). For each, call parseReceipt and assert that the returned merchant, date and total (or tax) fields match expectations, allowing optional fields to be undefined. Use the real parseReceipt implementation – no need to mock the extractor here.

Add __tests__/categories.test.ts: test default category list matches the spec, test adding a valid custom category, test that adding a duplicate (case‑insensitive) returns an error, test renaming a default category and that the new name appears in getAllCategories, test hiding a category and that it is excluded from getAllCategories when includeHidden is false, test that hideCategory fails when the category is used by a receipt (create a receipt first), test that syncCategoriesWithReceipts adds unknown receipt categories as custom entries, and finally test a backup round‑trip: create a store, add a receipt with a custom category, hide and rename some defaults, run createBackup, clear store, restoreBackup, then verify that the restored categories match the saved state and that the receipt still has its original category string.

Run the full TypeScript compilation (npx tsc --noEmit) and Jest unit suite to ensure no existing tests break. Adjust any import paths needed for the new modules, export them from appropriate index files if the project uses barrel exports, and add any missing type definitions.

Update package.json to include the new runtime dependencies: "expo-text-extractor": "^2.0.0" and "react-native-paper-dates": "^0.24.1". No code changes are required for the CI because the Jest mock will intercept the native module, and the date picker component is pure JS/TS and already listed as a peer dependency of react‑native‑paper.

Commit all changes, run npm ci, run linting, run the existing acceptance test runner (test_acceptance.py) to ensure all previous milestones still pass, and verify the new unit tests for OCR and categories also pass.
